BiblicalUsage: The word names desistance or desolation, and Jeremiah uses it once, when he would comfort himself against sorrow and his heart is faint within him. The comfort he reaches for will not come, and the word carries the weight of a grief that will not lift.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Jeremiah's faint heart is the honest prayer of a prophet who cannot comfort himself, and God hears it anyway.
